account: Today I have kept my office, market, lunch and accounts appointments. The unusual thing is repeated vague talk of a 'bridge or port change at inn,' which I heard from Townsfolk 03 and 23. I asked the secretary to investigate. She reports that the innkeeper neither proposed nor announced such a change and traces the rumor to Townsfolk 03. The baker says freight denied seeing any bridge or port change and offered only delivery help, warehouse space and ferry service. Builder reports the bridge passable with no confirmed defects, and the secretary relayed freight's reports of undamaged roads and a trouble-free ferry crossing. These are reports, not my own inspections. I do not yet know whether the rumor reflects a misunderstanding, ordinary discussion of transport services, or something more. There is no evidence so far of a secret plan or an actual route change. Bakery trade appears supplied: the baker reported seventy-two fresh loaves and asked whether gatherings would need bread; the secretary said none were listed today or tomorrow. At accounts, the secretary reported no receipts or expense claims and no agreed repair contract. I authorized no repair spending, and builder has agreed not to incur costs without approval and to submit written estimates for specific needs. It is now 14:00. I am awaiting the secretary's confirmation of the neighbour and dockside cottage for my 15:00 tea. That visit may also offer an ordinary opportunity to hear more firsthand local news.
